newsitem.title: USA: Arterial Vascular stock plunges on weak outlook.
newsitem.headline: Arterial Vascular stock plunges on weak outlook.

text.p: The stock of Arterial Vascular Engineering Inc. tumbled Friday, a day after the surgery products maker said it expected a sharp drop in second-quarter profits.
The stock slid $6.625 or almost 40 percent to $10 on Nasdaq at mid-afternoon.

The Santa Rosa, Calif.-based company, which makes coronary stent and balloon angioplasty products, said it expects earnings of 14 cents to 16 cents a share, well off from 25 cents a share, or $7.8 million, in the previous quarter.
Arterial Vascular blamed higher-than-expected expenses in the second quarter ending Dec. 31 and pricing pressure on its products for the earnings decline.

"Legal expenses have increased significantly as we continue to vigorously defend and pursue claims brought in connection with (our) purchase of technology from Endothelial Support Systems," said John Miller, chief financial officer.
Legal expenses, coupled with costs for terminating some distributorships, will total more than $1 million in the current quarter, he said.

Moreover, Arterial Vascular recently formed a direct sales force in several European countries and that has contributed to higher costs, while sales in those countries have been "significantly slower than anticipated," it added.
The company is boosting research and development costs and taking a charge of $400,000 in the quarter for a postponed stock offer. Those two factors also will contribute to the earnings shortfall.
